In this repository (/bench/repo — the Memos project, Go), markdown processing sits behind an interface (package internal/markdown, likely a `Service` interface).

Find precisely, with file:line:
1. The markdown interface definition — the `Service` interface (or similarly named) in internal/markdown/. List its methods and file:line.
2. Every concrete implementation of that interface that exists in the codebase (struct types implementing it). For each, give the type name and file:line. Identify which one(s) actually execute at runtime (i.e. are constructed and used by the running server, not just tests/mocks).
3. Who constructs the concrete implementation — the constructor function (e.g. NewService / NewGoldmarkService) and every production call site that creates it (file:line). Trace from server startup if possible (server/server.go, cmd/).
4. Which components/structs hold a reference to the interface (fields of type markdown.Service). List each holder struct, its field, and file:line — e.g. APIV1Service.MarkdownService, memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService, etc.

Report exact file paths and line numbers for the interface, the implementation(s), the constructor and its call sites, and every holder of the interface.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

32		// ExtractAll extracts tags, properties, and references in a single parse (most efficient)

I have all the information needed. Here is my complete report.

## Markdown Service — Interface, Implementation, Constructor, Holders

### 1. Interface definition
`Service` interface: **`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`** (doc comment at line 27).

Methods:
- `ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` — line 33
- `ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)` — line 36
- `ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)` — line 39
- `RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)` — line 42
- `RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)` — line 45
- `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` — line 48
- `ValidateContent(content []byte) error` — line 51
- `RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)` — line 54

### 2. Concrete implementation(s)
There is exactly **one** implementation in the entire codebase — no mocks, fakes, or alternate implementations exist.

- Type `service` (unexported struct, field `md goldmark.Markdown`): **`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:58`**. Its methods are defined at lines 143 (`ExtractTags`), 193 (`ExtractProperties`), 244 (`RenderMarkdown`), 255 (`RenderHTML`), 264 (`GenerateSnippet`), 349 (`ValidateContent`), 356 (`ExtractAll`), 425 (`RenameTag`).

This `service` type is the one that **executes at runtime** — it is the only concrete type, used by both tests and the running server.

### 3. Constructor and production call sites
Constructor: **`NewService(opts ...Option) Service`** at **`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`** (returns `&service{...}`).

Call sites:
- Production: **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48`**, inside `NewAPIV1Service` (lines 47–62), constructed with `WithTagExtension()` (line 49) and `WithMentionExtension()` (line 50) and stored into `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (line 56).
- Test only: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`.

Startup trace: `server/server.go:76` calls `apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)`, which internally calls `markdown.NewService(...)`. That single instance is then passed onward — e.g. `server/server.go:85` hands `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` to `rss.NewRSSService(...)`. So one `service` instance is shared across the running server.

### 4. Holders of `markdown.Service`
Production holder structs with a `markdown.Service` field:
- `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` — **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`** (set in constructor at v1.go:56).
- `RSSService.MarkdownService` — **`/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:45`** (constructor `NewRSSService` at rss.go:58, assigned at rss.go:62; used at rss.go:339 `RenderHTML`). Constructed in production at `server/server.go:85`.
- `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` — **`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`** (constructor `NewRunner` at runner.go:19, assigned at runner.go:22).

Note on the memopayload `Runner`: its constructor `memopayload.NewRunner` (runner.go:19) has **no production call sites** — the running server never builds this `Runner`. Instead the memopayload package is used in production via the free function **`RebuildMemoPayload(...)`** (runner.go:74), called directly with `s.MarkdownService` from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447`. So the live interface value flows APIV1Service.MarkdownService → RebuildMemoPayload, and APIV1Service.MarkdownService → RSSService.MarkdownService.

Test-only holder (not runtime): `fileserver_test.go:432` sets a `MarkdownService`, but there is no `markdown.Service` field in production fileserver code.
